original_question: How restrictive is the condition that the characteristic curves on a smooth hypersurface in standard symplectic space are planar?
target_in_paper: Serge Tabachnikov, subsection "Planar characteristic curves": for a (germ of a) smooth hypersurface in standard symplectic space, the paper asks how restrictive it is for the characteristic curves on M to be planar. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2602.12896))
correct_elements: Your draft is already very close to the paper's actual problem: it has the right ambient setting (standard symplectic space), the right object (a smooth hypersurface), the right geometric condition (planarity of characteristic curves), and the right intent (asking how restrictive that hypothesis is). ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2602.12896))
missing_details: The paper explicitly allows M to be a germ of a smooth hypersurface, so the scope is local as well as global. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2602.12896))
To be stand-alone, the ambient space should be written as the standard symplectic vector space (R^{2n}, ω_0). ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2602.12896))
The term "characteristic curves" should be defined as the integral curves of the characteristic line field ker(ω_0|_{TM}) on M.
The universal quantifier should be explicit: every characteristic curve on M is assumed planar.
The word "planar" should be made explicit as: each characteristic curve lies in some affine 2-plane of the ambient space.

The nearby context records the one concrete rigidity result motivating the question: if M is closed and convex, then M is an affine symplectic image of a round ball. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2602.12896))
refined_question: Let M be a germ of a smooth hypersurface in the standard symplectic vector space (R^{2n}, ω_0), and let its characteristic curves be the integral curves of the characteristic line field ker(ω_0|_{TM}). Assume that every characteristic curve of M is planar, i.e. each such curve is contained in an affine 2-plane of R^{2n}. How restrictive is this condition on M?
justification: The draft is essentially the paper's official problem, but the paper's wording contains one important scope condition—"(a germ of)"—and suppresses the standard definitions of the characteristic line field and planarity that are needed to make the question fully stand-alone. I therefore kept the problem at exactly the same level of generality and only unpacked those hidden definitions. I did not broaden it to classification of convex bodies, outer billiards, or any other neighboring topic. The only adjacent context I retained is the sentence immediately following the problem, which says that in the closed convex case the situation is rigid: M must be an affine symplectic image of a round ball. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2602.12896))
